newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent up on fund hedging, gas oil firmer.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent up on fund hedging, gas oil firmer.

text.p: IPE Brent futures were markedly higher early on Friday while gas oil also started stronger than expected.
July Brent was up 24 cents at $17.68 a barrel by 0945 GMT. July gas oil was $1.50 higher at $164 a tonne.
"There is a little bit of short covering going on. The funds have baled out of their longs and they don't want to be hurt again," one dealer said.
The push higher in the Brent price came as players reacted to figures showing North Sea loading programmes to be lower than expected.
The first of Norway's July loading programmes showed the Gullfaks system loading 21 cargoes, down three from June. Only a small increase in the July Brent loading programme was reported.
Prices were also buoyed by ongoing jitters about a delay in the second round of the Iraq/U.N. oil-for-food deal, brokers said.

The United Nations on Thursday said a team of its weapons inspectors had twice been blocked from entering a total of three suspected military sites since Tuesday, adding to worries that political posturing by Iraq over the distribution of food might delay the deal.
"It only takes one headline for people to sell at the moment," one dealer said. "Everyone is short of the market."
Gas oil was dragged higher by the rise in crude to outstip market expectations.
